compare_blocks.title: One-minute comparison

compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional company, either person can negotiate terms or protect a product commitment. Those responsibilities depend on the work and what each person has agreed to take on.

Intuition is the only shared letter. It describes a preference for noticing connections and possible outcomes. Either person can still check details and reach a different conclusion.

Compare each preference separately. E/I concerns attention and energy, T/F concerns decision criteria, and J/P concerns how someone engages with the outside world. Neither the task someone takes on nor how fast they decide can answer all three questions.

### ENTJ and INFP: on one cheap order, which condition is given up last

In this fictional order review, both people have the same costs, lead time, customer commitments and decision rights. They can apply the same criteria to every proposal and also ask what each option means for customers and staff.

One way to compare the options is to use consistent criteria for capacity, cost and quality. Another is to consider who would be affected if an existing order moved or a promise changed. The same decision can take both into account.

A promising new sales channel does not make an existing commitment disappear. An earlier promise does not by itself tell you whether the business can meet every obligation. Either person can ask which constraints apply to the decision.

Write the financial assumptions and existing commitments side by side. Check which are verified, which are open to negotiation, and which either proposal needs to honour.

### ENTJ and INFP: why only N is shared while both hold Fi and Te

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INFP is Fi–Ne–Si–Te. Both hold Te and Fi: Te is dominant for ENTJ and inferior for INFP, Fi is dominant for INFP and inferior for ENTJ, so the two names face each other at either end of the order.

Te and Fi are both judging processes in the model. Te describes applying external criteria to decisions. Fi describes evaluating choices against personally held values. Their positions do not measure care for others or predict how a disagreement will unfold.

The Foundation’s overview allows either attitude for the third process: Sensing for both types here. This page uses Se for ENTJ and Si for INFP. The dominant and auxiliary positions are unchanged. See the [ENTJ profile](/en/personality/entj) and [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp).

compare_blocks.body:
Boundary of use: what follows is two possible trade-offs inside the same order, not a method for typing anyone and not business advice. Put the cost assumptions and existing commitments on the same page. Ask what would need to change for an option to work, without assigning motives to either person.

One consideration is whether the order meets the same capacity, quality and margin criteria the company uses for comparable work. A possible future sales opportunity does not count as confirmed business.

Another consideration is what the change means for the customers and staff affected. If packaging changes, ask which commitments still need to be met and who would bear the consequences if more units arrived damaged.

Give both reviewers the same worksheet. Ask them to note the verified constraints, the commitments at stake and the information that could change their view. Either person may weigh both kinds of consideration.

A vacancy and a willingness to take it are separate questions. Discuss what the role involves, what other options exist and what changing jobs would mean for the person deciding.

Either partner can ask about pay, responsibilities, time and what would happen if the arrangement did not work. The decision to leave a job belongs to the person considering it.

Either partner might decline, consider a trial arrangement or propose another way to cover the work. The decision does not identify a type.

compare_blocks.body:
In a fictional company, either person can negotiate terms or protect a product commitment. Those responsibilities depend on the work and what each person has agreed to take on.

Intuition is the only shared letter. It describes a preference for noticing connections and possible outcomes. Either person can still check details and reach a different conclusion.

sections.title: Quick answer

sections.body_md:
In a fictional company, either person can negotiate terms or protect a product commitment. Those responsibilities depend on the work and what each person has agreed to take on.

Intuition is the only shared letter. It describes a preference for noticing connections and possible outcomes. Either person can still check details and reach a different conclusion.

Compare each preference separately. E/I concerns attention and energy, T/F concerns decision criteria, and J/P concerns how someone engages with the outside world. Neither the task someone takes on nor how fast they decide can answer all three questions.

### ENTJ and INFP: on one cheap order, which condition is given up last

In this fictional order review, both people have the same costs, lead time, customer commitments and decision rights. They can apply the same criteria to every proposal and also ask what each option means for customers and staff.

One way to compare the options is to use consistent criteria for capacity, cost and quality. Another is to consider who would be affected if an existing order moved or a promise changed. The same decision can take both into account.

A promising new sales channel does not make an existing commitment disappear. An earlier promise does not by itself tell you whether the business can meet every obligation. Either person can ask which constraints apply to the decision.

Write the financial assumptions and existing commitments side by side. Check which are verified, which are open to negotiation, and which either proposal needs to honour.

### ENTJ and INFP: why only N is shared while both hold Fi and Te

In the common four-function notation used here, ENTJ is Te–Ni–Se–Fi and INFP is Fi–Ne–Si–Te. Both hold Te and Fi: Te is dominant for ENTJ and inferior for INFP, Fi is dominant for INFP and inferior for ENTJ, so the two names face each other at either end of the order.

Te and Fi are both judging processes in the model. Te describes applying external criteria to decisions. Fi describes evaluating choices against personally held values. Their positions do not measure care for others or predict how a disagreement will unfold.

The Foundation’s overview allows either attitude for the third process: Sensing for both types here. This page uses Se for ENTJ and Si for INFP. The dominant and auxiliary positions are unchanged. See the [ENTJ profile](/en/personality/entj) and [INFP profile](/en/personality/infp).

In this fictional comparison, both people have the same inquiry, capacity, delivery deadline, customer terms and decision rights. Every row compares possible emphases under those shared conditions.

Either person can use either column. A possible emphasis cannot identify a type.

| Shared situation | ENTJ: possible emphasis | INFP: possible emphasis | Preference illustrated |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Both weigh the same confirmed order terms | Whether those terms meet the same capacity, price and quality criteria | How those terms affect staff, customers and existing commitments | T/F · Decision criteria |
| Both compare the same options after a request for a discount | Whether each option meets the criteria applied to comparable orders | Whether each option respects the commitments already made to the people affected | T/F · Decision criteria |
| Both have the same three-week deadline and full production schedule | Record a working plan and identify what would justify changing it | Keep feasible schedules open while checking the same constraints | J/P · Outward approach |
| Both hear the same objection and have the same time to consider it | Clarify what the objection means through discussion | Clarify what the objection means through private reflection | E/I · Direction of attention |
| Both hear the same suggestion of future orders | Consider what new opportunities might follow if the customer returns | Consider what new opportunities might follow if the customer returns | Shared N · This cannot distinguish the types |
| Both review the same delivery results to plan for next time | Record a provisional approach and what would reopen it | Keep feasible approaches open until the remaining questions are answered | J/P · Outward approach |

Either person can examine the terms, ask about quality or form a plan. Experience, responsibility and access to information can shape what they raise. No row measures competence.
sections.title: ENTJ and INFP in one minute

sections.body_md:
Boundary of use: what follows is two possible trade-offs inside the same order, not a method for typing anyone and not business advice. The quantity, margin and lead time are invented and serve only as practice; a real decision about taking work rests on the contract, the capacity and the cash-flow figures, and legal and tax questions belong with the relevant professionals.

Put the cost assumptions and existing commitments on the same page. Ask what would need to change for an option to work, without assigning motives to either person.

### ENTJ and INFP: Weighing a low-margin order

In this fictional example, a customer asks for 30,000 units with three weeks to deliver. The quoted margin is 6%, and the line is already booked. Both reviewers know which existing orders could be affected and what they have promised those customers.

One consideration is whether the order meets the same capacity, quality and margin criteria the company uses for comparable work. A possible future sales opportunity does not count as confirmed business.

Another consideration is what the change means for the customers and staff affected. If packaging changes, ask which commitments still need to be met and who would bear the consequences if more units arrived damaged.

The fictional team can compare the options with both sets of considerations visible. The example does not recommend accepting at a particular price or reducing quality checks.

Give both reviewers the same worksheet. Ask them to note the verified constraints, the commitments at stake and the information that could change their view. Either person may weigh both kinds of consideration.

### ENTJ and INFP: should a partner quit their job to help

In this fictional example, the company needs help and one partner asks whether the other would consider leaving their job to run operations. The two can discuss what the business needs and whether the role suits the person’s interests and circumstances.

A vacancy and a willingness to take it are separate questions. Discuss what the role involves, what other options exist and what changing jobs would mean for the person deciding.

Either partner can ask about pay, responsibilities, time and what would happen if the arrangement did not work. The decision to leave a job belongs to the person considering it.

Either partner might decline, consider a trial arrangement or propose another way to cover the work. The decision does not identify a type.

sections.body_md:
When results differ, compare the assessment, language version and scoring. Then consider which experiences came to mind, including choices you made freely and decisions your role required.

For reflection, compare similar decisions where you had genuine discretion. Note whether conversation or private reflection helped, which criteria mattered, and whether you settled an outward plan or left options open. Keep the three questions separate.

The notes help you reflect on particular decisions. They cannot score a preference, determine a type or establish why an assessment result changed.
